tutorial.step2Title: Sourcing request: an agent does the work
tutorial.step2Body: No standard product fits? Describe what you need; a SourcingPick agent qualifies the brief, tenders 3 to 10 pre-screened factories, and forwards you the quotes. You pick the winner.

tutorial.step4Body: Every payment moves through our escrow account. The factory is only paid after you confirm delivery. If a dispute arises, funds stay frozen until arbitration.

bodies.invoicing:
Hi,

Here's how invoicing works on SourcingPick: each order generates a deposit invoice (30–50% of total, depending on the factory) when it goes into production, then a balance invoice at shipment. Both are downloadable from your dashboard and compliant with EU requirements. Let me know if you have any questions.
bodies.guarantees:
Hi,

Product guarantees: 1) compliance with the specs accepted in the quote (QC photos shared before shipping); 2) a 7-day dispute window after confirmed delivery to flag any defect; 3) the escrow covers refunds if a dispute is resolved in your favour. Factory-quoted lead times are firm — any delay over 7 days triggers a flag to our team.
bodies.refunds:
Hi,

Refund policy: if a dispute is opened within 7 days of delivery, our team arbitrates within 5 business days. Three possible outcomes: full refund (custom product off-spec), partial 80% (standard product off-spec), or motivated refusal. Funds stay in escrow while the dispute is open.
bodies.deposit_balance:
Hi,

Payment runs in two stages: 1) a deposit at order time (30–50% of total, set by the factory) that kicks off production; 2) the balance at shipment. Both move via bank wire to our escrow account — we only release to the factory after delivery is confirmed. Full breakdown is on your Order page.
bodies.research_process:
Hi,

Supplier research process: 1) you submit a request describing what you need; 2) a SourcingPick agent is assigned and qualifies the brief; 3) they may bill a research fee (€125/day depending on scope) — payable upfront, refundable as platform credit if no result is found within the agreed timeframe; 4) they tender 3 to 10 pre-screened factories and forward you the quotes. You keep final-acceptance control.

bodies.how_it_works:
Hi,

Here's how it works:

1. You send us a request describing what you need — specs, quantity, target price and deadline.
2. One of our agents in China qualifies it and approaches suitable factories.
3. You receive a quote covering the product, the checks and the delivery terms.
4. If you accept, your payment is held in escrow and released only once conforming delivery is confirmed.

Happy to walk through a specific project whenever you're ready.
bodies.pricing:
Hi,

There's no subscription — we're paid on successful transactions.

Sourcing (agent-led, custom production): 4% of order value from the buyer, 1% from the supplier. A research fee of €125/day covers the qualification work before sourcing starts, and it's credited back as platform credit if you place an order within 30 days.

Marketplace (ready catalogue, one-click): 2% from the buyer — already included in the listed price, so there's nothing added at checkout — and 1% from the seller.

Shipping is quoted separately.

Happy to break this down for a specific order.
bodies.lead_times:
Hi,

For a fully secured order — including production, quality checks and air freight — plan on at least 31 days from acceptance of the quote.

Shorter is sometimes possible, but it usually means giving up one of the checks, so we'd rather tell you up front than surprise you later. Tell us your deadline and we'll say honestly whether it's realistic.
bodies.china_only:
Hi,

SourcingPick currently sources from China. Our agents are on the ground there, speak the language and visit the factories in person — which is what makes the checks worth anything.

More countries will open later. If your project needs another origin today, we'd rather say so than take it on and disappoint you.
bodies.become_supplier:
Hi,

Thanks for your interest in selling through SourcingPick.

To register you'll need your business licence (营业执照). Your unified social credit code (统一社会信用代码) is what identifies your company on the platform.

For verification we additionally need the ID of a company representative holding more than 25% of the capital.

You can start the registration from our site, and we'll come back to you once the documents are reviewed.
bodies.marketplace_buy:
Hi,

Marketplace listings are products we've already negotiated and checked, so you can order them directly without going through a sourcing request.

The price you see is the price you pay — our commission is already included. Payment is held in escrow and released to the supplier only once delivery is confirmed.

Tell us what you're looking for and we'll point you to the right listings.
bodies.vehicles:
Hi,

Our vehicle listings show make, model, year, mileage, fuel, gearbox and — importantly — whether a Certificate of Conformity (CoC) is available.

That last one matters: without a CoC the vehicle cannot be registered in the EU, so we state it plainly on every listing rather than leaving you to find out later.

Tell us what you're after and we'll send you what matches.
bodies.create_account:
Hi,

To place a request, follow an order or talk to us about a specific transaction, you'll need an account — that's what lets us tie the conversation to your company and your orders.

Signing up takes a couple of minutes. Once you're in, message us from your dashboard and we'll pick up right where we left off here.

items.question: How much does it cost to sell on SourcingPick?
items.answer: There's no subscription and no listing fee. We deduct a 1% commission from your payout only when an order completes. Nothing upfront, nothing if you don't sell.

items.question: When and how do I get paid?
items.answer: Buyer funds sit in the SourcingPick Wise escrow account from the moment they wire. On confirmed, conforming delivery, your net amount (order value minus the 1%) is sent to your bank account in 1–3 business days.

items.question: What role does Wise play in this?
items.answer: Wise hosts the platform-side escrow account and executes payouts to your bank. You enter your bank details once (IBAN, SWIFT, or Chinese local account) and every payout arrives there automatically at the mid-market rate.

items.question: What's the difference between marketplace, custom, sourcing, and auctions?
items.answer: Marketplace: your ready-to-ship products, bought in one click. Custom orders: tender-and-quote work negotiated by an agent against a buyer spec. Sourcing: a dedicated agent searches suppliers for the buyer, paid via a research fee. Auctions (coming soon): sell large batches or clearance stock to the highest bidder.

items.question: How does a marketplace order play out?
items.answer: Buyer picks your product → wires the deposit to the SourcingPick Wise account (escrow) → you receive the order, run QC, upload QC photos, ship with a tracking number → on confirmed delivery your net payout is released.

items.question: How does a custom order play out?
items.answer: An agent invites you to quote against a brief. If the buyer accepts your quote, an order is created with a 30–50% deposit (matching what you proposed in the quote), then the balance on delivery. The escrow flow is identical.

items.question: What happens if there's a dispute?
items.answer: Funds stay in the Wise escrow. SourcingPick acts as the mediator — we review your QC photos, shipment proofs, and the full messaging thread. For a confirmed product defect, we negotiate a partial refund and the platform absorbs part of the cost alongside you. For custom orders that don't meet spec, a larger refund may apply. You're not on your own.

items.question: How are buyers vetted?
items.answer: Every sourcing request is reviewed and qualified by a SourcingPick agent before any factory is invited. Marketplace buyers wire through Wise escrow like everyone else — you're never exposed to non-payment.

items.question: Do I need certifications to sell?
items.answer: Not mandatory, but buyers can filter on them — listing your real certifications (GOTS, OEKO-TEX, FSC, CE…) gets you in front of more serious orders.

items.question: What do I need to get verified (KYC)?
items.answer: Your business registration, a tax document, and one or two facility photos. Verification is one-time and usually quick.

about.title: Sourcing shouldn't be an act of faith.
body: SourcingPick exists because international procurement, in 2026, is still a chain of patience, WhatsApp threads, and wire transfers in the dark. Buyers pay upfront to suppliers they've never met. Factories accept specs they haven't had time to qualify. The opaque middleman pockets the difference.

We're building the opposite: a platform where every request is qualified by a human, every quote is compared on the same scoring grid, and every payment stays in escrow until confirmed delivery. The platform's margin is transparent, not buried in the price.
We're based in France and our factory network is currently concentrated in China. Our agents are on the ground, speak your suppliers' language and work in their time zone.

sections.heading: Acceptance of terms
body: By accessing SourcingPick or creating an account, you agree to be bound by these terms of service. If you do not accept these terms, you must not use the service.

sections.heading: Description of the service
body: SourcingPick is a SaaS platform that connects buyers ("Clients") with manufacturers ("Factories") through three main services: on-demand sourcing, a marketplace of pre-negotiated products, and a certification programme.
SourcingPick acts as a trusted third party and operates a funds-escrow mechanism via a licensed payment provider.

sections.heading: Accounts and verification
body: Account creation is free. Each organisation must provide accurate, up-to-date information and complete a verification (KYC) procedure before transacting.
You are responsible for the confidentiality of your credentials. Any activity carried out from your account is presumed to be yours.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
body: You may not use SourcingPick for illegal or fraudulent activities, or activities contrary to French and European regulations on international trade, labour law, or intellectual property.
Any circumvention of the escrow mechanism, the certification programme, or our verification tools is strictly prohibited.

sections.heading: Payments, commissions, and escrow
body: Funds paid by Clients are collected by our payment provider and held in escrow until the buyer confirms conforming receipt of the goods.
SourcingPick takes a commission on each transaction. The rate depends on the subscribed plan and is disclosed at quote time.

sections.heading: Intellectual property
body: All elements of the platform (software, design, trademarks, editorial content) are the exclusive property of SourcingPick or its licensors.
You retain all rights in the content you publish (specifications, photos, documents) and grant SourcingPick a limited licence to use it for operating the service.

sections.heading: Warranties and limitation of liability
body: SourcingPick takes all reasonable steps to vet its partner factories but cannot guarantee absolute conformity of manufactured products. The escrow mechanism is designed precisely to protect the buyer in case of non-conformity.
Our liability is limited, to the extent permitted by law, to the amount actually received in respect of the affected transaction.

sections.heading: Termination
body: You may terminate your account at any time from your settings. SourcingPick may suspend or terminate an account in case of breach of these terms, after notice.

sections.heading: Changes to the terms
body: We may modify these terms to reflect changes in the service or in regulations. Any material change will be notified to you by email at least 30 days before it takes effect.

sections.heading: Governing law and jurisdiction
body: These terms are governed by French law. Any dispute shall fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Paris Court of Appeal, subject to mandatory legal provisions to the contrary.

sections.heading: Contact

sections.heading: Data controller
body: SourcingPick SAS, headquartered in France, is the controller of personal data collected via the platform. To exercise your rights or contact our Data Protection Officer: dpo@sourcingpick.com.

sections.heading: Data we collect
body: Account data: first name, last name, email, phone, preferred language, role, and parent organisation.
Organisation data: legal name, registration number, VAT number, address, bank details, KYC documents.
Usage data: login history, requests created, quotes received, orders, messages exchanged.

sections.heading: Purposes and legal bases
body: Contract performance: delivery of the sourcing service, processing of orders and payments.
Legal obligations: KYC compliance, anti-money-laundering, invoicing, accounting retention.
Legitimate interest: platform security, fraud prevention, service improvement.
Consent: audience measurement, marketing communications (where you explicitly opt in).

sections.heading: Data sharing
body: We share certain data with technical service providers under contract (hosting, email, payments, KYC) acting as processors under GDPR.
We never sell your data. We may be required to disclose it to competent authorities under legal obligation.

sections.heading: Retention periods
body: Account data: kept while your account is active, then archived for 3 years after the last transaction.
KYC documents: kept for 5 years after the end of the business relationship, per AML-CFT obligations.
Invoicing data: kept for 10 years, per the French Commercial Code.

sections.heading: Your rights (GDPR)
body: You have rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, and objection regarding your personal data. You can exercise these from your settings or by writing to dpo@sourcingpick.com.
In case of disagreement, you may lodge a complaint with the CNIL (www.cnil.fr).

sections.heading: International transfers
body: Our primary infrastructure is hosted in the European Union. When processing an order involves partners outside the EU, we apply the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses to govern the transfers.

sections.heading: Cookies
body: Our use of cookies is detailed in our dedicated cookies policy.

sections.heading: Security
body: Sensitive data (passwords, IBANs, KYC documents) are encrypted at rest. Access is restricted on a need-to-know basis and logged. Two-factor authentication is mandatory for Admin accounts.

sections.heading: Contact
body: Data Protection Officer: dpo@sourcingpick.com.

sections.heading: What is a cookie?
body: A cookie is a small text file placed on your device when you visit a website. It lets the site remember certain information (language, login session, consent choice) between visits.

sections.heading: Strictly necessary cookies
body: These cookies are essential to the platform's operation and do not require your prior consent.
sp_locale (1 year) — remembers your preferred language.
sp_consent (1 year) — records your choice regarding non-essential cookies.
next-auth.session-token (session) — keeps you signed in while authenticated.
next-auth.csrf-token (session) — protects authentication forms against CSRF attacks.

sections.heading: Non-essential cookies
body: In the current version, SourcingPick does not set any non-essential cookies. If we introduce analytics or marketing tools in the future, they will only be set after your explicit consent via the dedicated banner.

sections.heading: Managing your choices
body: You can change your choice at any time by deleting the sp_consent cookie from your browser settings, then reloading the page: the consent banner will reappear.
You can also block or delete all cookies via your browser settings. Note that this may affect certain features of the service (notably authentication).

sections.heading: Contact
body: For any question about our use of cookies: dpo@sourcingpick.com.

sections.heading: Our stance, plainly
body: SourcingPick handles financial and personal data: factory KYC, bank details, invoices, buyer credentials. We built the platform with security as a first-class constraint without claiming an ISO 27001 or SOC 2 certification we haven't earned.

This page is a candid read: what's in place technically, what's in place around governance, and what's on the roadmap. It's updated whenever something material changes — the version below reflects the state as of {{lastUpdated}}.
If you represent an enterprise buyer or compliance team and need deeper material (DPIA, RIA, SIG Lite, etc.), email security@sourcingpick.com.

sections.heading: Technical controls in place
body: Role isolation — every protected path passes through a requireRole() guard plus org-membership checks. No path trusts the proxy alone.
Audit log — every sensitive action (KYC, payment, auction edit, pre-tender rejection) writes an AuditLog row with actor, payload and level (INFO/WARN/ALERT). Retained indefinitely in DB.
Authentication — Auth.js v5 with bcrypt passwords, optional TOTP OTP, forwarder magic-link (#15). Sessions use signed HTTP-only tokens, SameSite=Lax.

Payments — Wise Business escrow (sole rail since 2026-06). Wise webhooks are RSA-signed, persisted in WebhookEvent, and replayable from the admin UI. Idempotency on providerRef stops double-settlement.
Attachments — typed (image/video/audio/file), per-context cap, mime sniffed at upload. Forwarder magic links carry TTL + revoke controls.
Factory-price confidentiality — the platform margin and the factory price are never exposed to the buyer (two-tier quote shape).

sections.heading: Data and hosting
body: Hosting in Europe (Paris / Frankfurt depending on stack tier). Data encrypted at rest via the provider's disk layer; DB connections over TLS.
Personal data falls under GDPR: we act as controller for user accounts (client, factory, agent, admin) and as processor for content exchanged between buyers and factories.
Primary sub-processors: Wise Business (payments), our hosting provider, our transactional email provider. The detailed list is available on request to security@sourcingpick.com.

sections.heading: Governance & incident handling
body: Not yet ISO 27001 or SOC 2 certified. Our target is a SOC 2 Type 1 audit within 12 months of v1 launch.
Incident reporting: security@sourcingpick.com. We commit to a response within 24 business hours and notification of affected individuals within GDPR's 72-hour window where applicable.
Informal bug bounty: no dedicated platform yet — disclose vulnerabilities responsibly to security@sourcingpick.com and we'll engage in good faith.

sections.heading: What we're actively working on
body: ISMS authoring kicked off; SOC 2 pre-audit prep in flight.
Annual external penetration tests — first pass scheduled for 2026-Q4.
Secret rotation policy + centralised credentials vault (HashiCorp Vault or equivalent).
ISO 27001 Statement of Applicability — drafting to anchor enterprise procurement questionnaires.

faq.title: What to know before you source through us.
faq.intro: Four products, one platform. Pick the section that fits your situation to understand how it works, who pays what, and what happens when something goes wrong.
faq.contactPrompt: Can't find your answer? Write to

sourcing.heading: Agent-led sourcing
sourcing.intro: The flagship flow: you describe the need, an agent qualifies it and runs a tender across pre-vetted factories, you get comparable quotes scored on the same grid.

items.q: How does the agent pick which factories to invite?
items.a: By category, region and required certifications. Every factory in the pool is KYC-verified (registration, export licence, sample product). The agent prioritises those whose track record matches your brief.

items.q: How long until I see the quotes?
items.a: Target 24 business hours for qualification, then 5 to 7 days to gather quotes (depending on brief complexity and the factory's time zone).

items.q: Is there an upfront research fee?
items.a: On highly specific requests the agent may charge a research fee (€125/day). It's credited back in full toward your order if you accept a quote within 30 days of paying it.

items.q: Can I edit my request after sending it?
items.a: Yes until the tender goes out — ping your agent. Once factories have been invited, any material change resets the quote round.

items.q: What if none of the quotes work for me?
items.a: Reject them all at no cost (excluding any research fee already paid). The agent can re-tender with a refined brief if you'd like.

marketplace.heading: Marketplace — ready-to-ship stock
marketplace.intro: Catalogue of products already in stock at our partner factories. You buy directly, no agent in the loop, with payment split into two stages.

items.q: How is this different from a B2C site?
items.a: Prices are net of VAT, MOQ and lead times are shown on every listing, and payment sits in our Wise escrow until you confirm conforming delivery.

items.q: When am I charged?
items.a: 30% deposit at checkout, 70% balance on shipment. Both payments land in our escrow IBAN.

items.q: Can the factory change price or stock after I order?
items.a: No. Once your order is in, the price and terms are locked. If the factory can't honour it, the order is cancelled and the deposit refunded in full.

items.q: Can I order below MOQ?
items.a: Not on the marketplace. For smaller quantities or a variant, start a sourcing request instead.

auctions.heading: Auctions — batches and clearance lots
auctions.intro: Factories list lots for sale by bidding. Highest bid at close wins; some lots include a buy-now price for instant purchase.

items.q: How does the commission work on auctions?
items.a: A progressive 10%–15% curve depending on the final amount. It comes out of the factory's settlement, never added to your bid.

items.q: What happens if I win?
items.a: An order is created on your dashboard with a 30% deposit / 70% balance schedule, payable by Wise wire.

items.q: What if I'm outbid at the last second?
items.a: You get an instant notification with a link to bid again. Minimum increment between bids is €1.

items.q: What if no one meets the reserve?
items.a: The lot goes unsold — no order is created and no one is charged. The factory can relist it.

items.q: Can I cancel an auction I've won?
items.a: No. A winning bid is legally binding. Cancelling means losing the deposit and a flag on your profile.

custom.heading: Custom production
custom.intro: For products that aren't on the marketplace or in auctions: bespoke tooling, custom packaging, validation samples. Always via the agent-led sourcing path.

items.q: What's the minimum lead time for a custom run?
items.a: 31 calendar days at the factory + transit. Below that we can't guarantee quality or the validation chain. The platform warns you in the request wizard.

items.q: What deposit is required for custom?
items.a: The factory chooses 30%–50% at quote time. It's higher than the marketplace because the factory commits raw materials and tooling before anything ships.

items.q: Can I validate a sample before the full run?
items.a: Yes, and we recommend it. The quote can include a separately-priced sample; full production starts after your written sign-off.

items.q: Who owns the IP of designs I share?
items.a: You do, fully. Partner factories agree to a no-reuse clause on customer designs via the platform's terms.

disputes.heading: Disputes, returns and responsibilities
disputes.intro: Our Wise escrow lets us freeze final settlement while a dispute is open. Here's who pays what when things go wrong.

items.q: How long do I have to open a dispute?
items.a: 7 calendar days from declared conforming delivery. After that, the balance is released to the factory automatically.

items.q: Who decides if there's a disagreement?
items.a: Our support team arbitrates based on photos, certificates and messages from the order thread. The decision is communicated in writing to both sides.

items.q: Sourcing/custom: who pays for non-conformity?
items.a: The factory covers replacement or full refund if non-conformity vs. the signed quote is proven. Agent and platform fees are refunded pro-rata.

items.q: Marketplace: what if the product doesn't match the listing?
items.a: You get a full refund (deposit + shipping already paid). The factory loses access to publishing until the dispute is closed.

items.q: Auctions: is the guarantee the same?
items.a: For lots described as "new", yes. For clearance / used lots, the guarantee is limited to material non-conformity (dead stock, counterfeit, false claims). Read the lot description carefully before bidding.

items.q: Is the platform liable in any way?
items.a: Yes for intermediation and payment security. No for hidden manufacturing defects outside the qualification scope — the factory remains responsible for production.
